newsitem.title: FRANCE: Bomb defused at French papal visit church.
newsitem.headline: Bomb defused at French papal visit church.

text.p: Bomb disposal experts defused a home-made bomb in a church in western France which Pope John Paul is due to visit this month, police said on Tuesday.

The device was discovered on Monday night at a saint's tomb in the basilica of Saint-Laurent-sur-Sevre, a village 60 km (35 miles) east of Nantes, where the pontiff is due to pray on September 19. A slogan hostile to the papal visit was daubed on the wall, police said.

The parish priest in the rural village discovered the bomb at the tomb of Saint Louis-Marie Grignion de Monfort, an 18th century missionary from whose writings Pope John Paul draws his Latin motto "totus tuus" (I am all yours), a symbol of devotion to the Virgin Mary.
The priest immediately alerted police. The local government prefect's office said the bomb was made with explosives commonly used in road-building.
No one has claimed responsibility. The public prosecutor's office in La-Roche-sur-Yon, the capital of the Vendee region, opened an investigation.
The pope's September 19-22 visit to France has stirred opposition both by militant secularists and among Roman Catholics hostile to his conservative teachings on birth control, abortion and AIDS.
